title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 8
paragraphs: “Persians, I shall not be the first to establish this custom in your nation; having received it from others, I shall follow it. As I am told by those older than myself, we have never kept still since we received this supremacy, succeeding the Medes when Cyrus overthrew Astyages; so God leads us, and our own busy activity on many fronts tends to our good. As for the nations whom Cyrus and Cambyses and my father Darius subdued and added to their possessions, I need not tell you — you know them well. As for myself, from the day I inherited this throne on which I sit, I have considered carefully how in this honored position I might not fall short of those who have come before me, nor add less power to Persia than they did. And as I considered, I find a way by which we may win not only glory, together with a land no smaller or worse than the one we now hold — indeed more varied in its products — but also vengeance and retribution. I have called you together now so that I may share with you what I have in mind to do. I intend to yoke the Hellespont with a bridge and lead an army through Europe against Greece, so that I may take vengeance on the Athenians for all they have done to the Persians and to my father. You saw how my father Darius was preparing to march against these men; but he ended his life and did not manage to take his revenge. For his sake, then, and for the sake of the rest of the Persians, I will not stop until I have conquered Athens and burned it with fire — seeing that they wronged me and my father without provocation. First they came to Sardis in the company of our slave Aristagoras of Miletus and set fire to the sacred groves and the temples; and then, second, when we landed in their territory under the command of Datis and Artaphernes, you all know what they did to us. For these reasons I have resolved to make the campaign against them, and reckoning it up I find in the undertaking as many advantages as you shall hear. If we subdue these people and their neighbors, who dwell in the land of Pelops the Phrygian, we shall give Persia the same boundaries as the sky of Zeus; for in truth the sun will look down on no country that borders ours, since with your help I shall turn all the lands into one land, having passed through the whole length of Europe. For I am told that things are so: that there is no city of men, no people anywhere, that will be able to stand against us in battle once those I just mentioned have been removed. Thus both those who have done us wrong will wear the yoke of slavery, and those who have not. And you will please me best if you do this: whenever I give the signal of the time by which you must come, each of you must appear with zeal for the service; and whoever comes with the best-equipped force, to him I shall give the gifts reckoned most honorable in our country. This, then, is how it shall be done. But so that I may not seem to you to be following only my own counsel, I submit the matter for discussion, bidding any of you who so wishes to give his opinion.”
